lots.what_it_is: Nine pieces of 1970s-80s pub advertising ware: eight ceramic water jugs (Teacher's Scotch Whisky 'in a class of its own' black and gold, Gold Thimble Fine Old Scotch Whisky black square, The Black Douglas 8 Years Old Scotch Whisky black and gold, McCallum's maroon, Kaiser Stuhl Wines cream, Saltram 'Fine wine takes time' cream, a second plain-facing cream square jug, and an ochre character-face jug with 'Ch...' moulded on the base) plus an amber glass Chatelle Napoleon VSOP ashtray.
lots.score_reason: Common breweriana. Tasmanian evidence (Gowans) shows small groups of pub jugs selling for $6 to $25 hammer, and a single Wade Teacher's jug made $10 at a specialist breweriana sale. The whole lot is likely worth about $15 to $40 at auction.
lots.condition: From photos: glazes look clean and bright, gilt rims on Teacher's and Black Douglas look intact, no obvious chips or cracks visible, but backs and bases are not shown and small chips to spouts are common on these.
lots.key_photo_findings: All brand names read clearly in photos 1 to 3. Black Douglas jug reads '8 Years Old Scotch Whisky' with a gold medallion. The rear cream square jug's printed face is not shown. The character jug has moulded letters starting 'Ch' on the base, maker and brand not readable. No maker's marks (Wade, Elischer, Regicor) are visible because bases are not shown, so the researcher's maker attributions are unconfirmed.

sold.note: Page opened. Single Teacher's 'in a class of its own' jug, Wade base mark, 125 mm, some grime and minor scratches. Matches one of our nine pieces. Over 24 months old so cannot set a maximum bid; premium status not stated.

lots.dropped_entries: Gowans 'BOX OF SUNDRIES INCL DEWARS WATER JUG' $2 (listed 2026-07-12): figures confirmed but dropped as too weak a comparison (mixed sundries box). Auction Barn archive 1022 (10 June 2022): filed as UNSOLD but there is no evidence the lots were passed in, prices are simply hidden, so it is not an auction result of any kind; dropped (useful only as a maker reference). Also noted but not used: Gowans lot 400251 'BOX OF WHISKY JUGS & DEWARS FIGURE - DAMAGED' $190 hammer (listed 2026-03-30), a large box whose value was driven by a Dewar's piper figure.
lots.guide_summary: All surviving priced evidence used in the range is SOLD (AUD, no conversion): $6 to $25 hammer for groups of two to four pub jugs at Gowans, Hobart, and $10 for a single Teacher's jug at ABCR in 2022. No UNSOLD evidence. Two ASKING leads ($9.95 to $45 for single jugs) are snippet only and left out. A much larger 25-piece collection made $120 at Gowans, about $5 a piece.
lots.working: No SOLD sale is the same item (this nine-piece mix) in the last 24 months. The only exact-piece sale (ABCR Teacher's jug, $10) is from August 2022, outside 24 months. Gowans results are category guides or close-but-different groups. So keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0 under the rules. For context only: if the closest Gowans group ($11 for four pieces) were used, $11 / 1.22 = $9.02, rounded down = $5; a flip would need resale of say $40 for the lot less about 13% selling fees and nil postage (pickup) = $34.80 / 2.44 = $14.26, rounded down = $10, which is not worth the effort.
lots.confidence_reason: Brand labels read clearly in photos, and SOLD evidence pages and Gowans API data were opened, but there are no maker marks visible, the one exact-piece sale is from 2022, and the Tasmanian sales are category or close comparisons only.
